# informe gestion bdo 2025 english

<!-- página 1 -->

On the side of people that make things happen

          MANAGEMENT AND
        SUSTAINABILITY REPORT


<!-- página 2 -->

Presentation
| GRI 2-1 |


Banco de Occidente is a publicly traded company with securities
listed on the Colombian Stock Exchange for ordinary and
subordinated bonds. As of December 31, 2025, $3.20 trillion has
been issued and $3.10 trillion has been placed, of which $1.41
trillion of Series B bonds linked to the Consumer Price Index
(CPI) remain outstanding, with average issuance and maturity
terms of 2017 and 2029, respectively. As of the close of 2025, the
current issuance and placement program stands at $12.00 trillion,
with an available quota of $6.00 trillion to meet funding needs.
Additionally, Banco de Occidente’s shares are listed and traded
on the Colombian Stock Exchange as common stock.


  Main place of business:
  Santiago de Cali, Valle del Cauca.
  Main address:
  Carrera 4 # 7-61

Our History and Legacy
For 60 years, at Banco de Occidente we have evolved alongside Colombia, supporting the
development of people and businesses in a changing environment. Our history is marked by
expansion, innovation, a commitment to sustainability, and the continuous transformation of our
business, always maintaining closeness and trust as the pillars of our operation.

Reputation and
Recognition
Banco de Occidente’s reputation is the result of consistent
management, backed by financial strength, a commitment
to sustainability, talent development, innovation, and the
trust of our clients. In this regard, the awards, ratings, and
certifications we receive are not viewed merely as outcomes,
but as management inputs that allow us to evaluate
our performance, strengthen continuous improvement,
and guide actions to consolidate the Bank’s reputation
management.

Financial Strength
  BRC Standard & Poor’s
  In 2025, we hold a BRC 1+ rating, which represents the
  highest level of payment certainty for our short-term debt
  on a national scale.

  Fitch Ratings
  AAA (Colombia) rating for long-term debt, with a Stable
  outlook, and F1+ (Colombia) for short-term debt.

  Credit Consistency
  For the twenty-eighth consecutive year, we have maintained
  our AAA rating, which reflects the highest credit quality for
  our long-term debt in the Colombian market.

Business
Model
| GRI 2-6 |


Our business model is based on creating value for
our customers, shareholders, and other stakeholders
through financial solutions that meet the needs of a
dynamic and constantly changing environment. This
model rests on two fundamental pillars: Corporate
Banking and Retail Banking, each with distinct
offerings designed to provide high-quality financial
experiences and contribute to the sustainable
development of businesses and society.

                                                                                                                                  In 2025, we maintained our focus on driving economic
                                                                                                                                  growth that is both profitable and sustainable.
                                                                                                                                  We do this by creating value for our shareholders
                                                                                                                                  and customers, promoting the well-being of our
                                                                                                                                  employees and their families, and contributing to
                                                                                                                                  the country’s economic progress.
                                                                                                                                  The Vice Presidency of Finance and Strategy
                                                                                                                                  assumes a central responsibility: to protect the
                                                                                                                                  Bank’s assets and equity, as well as our customers’
                                                                                                                                  deposits. Building on this foundation, we contribute
                                                                                                                                  to growth through rigorous financial and tax
                                                                                                                                  planning, aimed at generating value and distributing
                                                                                                                                  it in a socially responsible manner, in line with our
                                                                                                                                  commitments to our stakeholders.

in a context influenced by the behavior of international interest rates.

In 2025, at Retail Banking, we remained committed
to people development, business growth, and the
country’s progress. It was a year of challenges—
including portfolio acquisitions, inflation that did not
behave as expected, and market liquidity needs—
but also of solid results and progress that drive us
to continue improving.

Alignment with the
Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs)
Our ESG strategy aligns with the United Nations
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as a reference
framework to guide our management and the Bank’s
contribution to the country’s sustainable development.
This alignment allows us to integrate economic, social,
and environmental considerations into decision-
making and ensure consistency between our strategy
and the initiatives we develop at the Bank.
In line with what was defined in the 2024 Management
and Sustainability Report, we maintain our focus
on the prioritized SDGs where, given the nature
of our financial activities, we can generate the
greatest impact. In this regard, our strategy
contributes primarily to SDG 8 (Decent Work and
Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and
Infrastructure), and SDG 13 (Climate Action), which
are integrated across the board into our business
decisions, risk management, internal operations, and
the development of sustainable financial solutions.
Complementarily, we contribute to other SDGs
through initiatives related to ethics and governance,
talent management, diversity and inclusion, customer
experience, and community engagement.

 Executive           Compensation for Senior Management at Banco de Occidente incorporates criteria linked to strategic performance and the management of risks relevant to the business, including environmental, social, and
 Compensation        governance (ESG) aspects. This approach aligns the decision-making of the Bank’s leaders with strategic objectives, business sustainability, and long-term value creation.
                     In 2025, incentive schemes incorporated criteria linked to prioritized material issues, consistent with the ESG strategy and the results of the double materiality analysis. Specifically, elements related to talent
                     management and development, emissions management and climate change, and information security, cybersecurity, and system availability were integrated into the evaluation of senior management’s
                     performance.
                     These criteria were applied through indicators related to leadership and capacity building, the management of climate risks and opportunities, and operational continuity and information protection. The design
                     and implementation of the compensation scheme were reviewed by internal governance bodies, in line with the Bank’s control and oversight framework.

                                                                                                                 Collective expertise of the highest governing body
                                                                                                                 | GRI 2 – 17|


                                                                                                                 During the reporting period, the governing body participated in various training sessions aimed at strengthening
                                                                                                                 its collective knowledge on matters relevant to business oversight. The training sessions addressed topics such
                                                                                                                 as sustainability and international standards applicable to the financial sector, climate risks and their impact
                                                                                                                 on credit risk management, artificial intelligence and data analytics, cybersecurity and data privacy, as well
                                                                                                                 as regulations and corporate governance practices. These activities helped strengthen the understanding of
                                                                                                                 the financial, regulatory, and operational impacts necessary for informed decision-making.

                                                                                          Senior Management
                                                                                          | GRI 2-13 |


                                                                                          Senior Management is responsible for the administration of the Bank and leads the execution of the corporate strategy, integrating sustainability
                                                                                          practices into daily management that strengthen value creation for the organization and our stakeholders. It is headed by the President and
                                                                                          comprises the Vice Presidents, who periodically report to the Board of Directors on progress and results, and, together with the Board, reports
                                                                                          to the General Shareholders’ Meeting on performance and achievements, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Three of the Code
                                                                                          of Good Corporate Governance, regarding the mechanisms for evaluating and controlling the activities of administrators, senior executives,
                                                                                          and directors. The Office of the Ombudsman, as well as the Audit, Treasury, and Compliance departments, also support the President in his
                                                                                          management duties.
                                                                                          At the Board of Directors meeting on January 10, 2025, the resignation of Iván Mauricio Ricardo Arias was accepted, and the appointment of
                                                                                          Carlos Andrés Echeverri as Vice President of Companies was approved. On that same day, the Board accepted the resignation of Pedro Luis
                                                                                          Villegas, and on March 6, 2025, Mario Botina Tovar was appointed Vice President of Operations and Technology. Subsequently, on September
                                                                                          12, the resignation of Mr. Eduardo Alfonso Correo was accepted, and the appointment of Ángela María Ceballos as Vice President of Human
                                                                                          Resources and Administration was approved. Finally, at the meeting on September 26, 2025, the resignation of Douglas Berrío Zapata was
                                                                                          accepted, and the appointment of Juana Beltrán Echeverri as Vice President of Legal Affairs was approved.


                                                                                               A significant milestone in 2025 regarding diversity and inclusion was the appointment of two women
                                                                                               to vice-presidential positions, strengthening female representation in senior management and
                                                                                               broadening the diversity of perspectives in decision-making. In this context, the Board of Directors
                                                                                               approved the appointment of Ángela María Ceballos as Vice President of Human Resources and
                                                                                               Administration and of Juana Beltrán Echeverri as Vice President of Legal Affairs, marking concrete
                                                                                               progress toward a more diverse, balanced, and representative leadership.

                                                                                                                   Regulatory and Legal
                                                                                                                   Compliance
                                                                                                                                      SDG 16.5; 16.6; 17.5
                                                                                                                                      | GRI 2-27 |


                                                                                                                   Regulatory and legal compliance is a cornerstone of financial security that underpins trust and credibility
                                                                                                                   with our customers, shareholders, authorities, and other stakeholders. At Banco de Occidente, we work
                                                                                                                   to anticipate regulatory changes, ensure the timely application of current legal requirements, and
                                                                                                                   maintain controls that support transparent, ethical, and responsible management. We emphasize that
                                                                                                                   the Bank is supported by a robust governance and control structure, which has not been implicated
                                                                                                                   in insider trading, antitrust violations, unfair competition practices, market manipulation, malpractice,
                                                                                                                   or other regulatory breaches within the financial industry.
                                                                                                                   Therefore, during the reporting period, there were no instances of significant non-compliance with
                                                                                                                   applicable laws or regulations. Consequently, the total number of significant non-compliance cases
                                                                                                                   reported in 2025 was 0, with the following breakdown:
                                                                                                                    Cases resulting in fines                                                                       0
                                                                                                                    Cases resulting in non-monetary sanctions                                                      0
                                                                                                                    Cases involving insider trading, antitrust violations, unfair competition
                                                                                                                    practices, market manipulation, malpractice, or other regulatory violations                    0
                                                                                                                    within the financial industry

                                                                                                                   Regarding the description of cases, to date no significant non-compliance has been identified for
                                                                                                                   the 2025 reporting period; therefore, there are no events to describe in this section. To determine what
                                                                                                                   constitutes a “significant non-compliance,” the Bank relies on its risk management methodology,
                                                                                                                   particularly in the management of operational risk, which includes legal risk. This approach allows for
                                                                                                                   the assessment of the materiality and potential severity of events, as well as their impact on the Bank
                                                                                                                   and its stakeholders, ensuring consistency in the analysis and traceability of the report.

Our Board of Directors assumes responsibility for identifying and understanding the risks associated with
corruption. Within this framework, it approves the Internal and External Fraud Management Policy and
monitors its implementation. Periodically, it receives clear, comprehensive, and timely information on the
assessment of these risks, based on defined criteria that promote continuous improvement.

To manage these risks, we operate under a three-lines-of-defense model, designed so that each team has
clarity regarding its role and knows how to contribute to safeguarding the Bank’s integrity:

                                                                                                                        Water Consumption
                                                                                                                        Measuring water consumption is a central pillar of our water resource management. To this end, we consolidate
                                                                                                                        data through the Energy Master platform, where we record and analyze consumption at our operational sites
                                                                                                                        based on water utility bills, thereby enhancing data traceability and reliability for decision-making.

                                                                                                                        *Figures in millions of cubic meters (M³).


                                                                                                                             The trend in water consumption reflects the strengthening of our water resource management and
                                                                                                                             the progressive improvement in the quality of reported information. In 2025, the Bank’s total water
                                                                                                                             consumption was 0,0398 M³, representing a 19,52% increase compared to 2024.
                                                                                                                             This increase should be interpreted in the context of adjustments to data coverage and the consolidation
                                                                                                                             of complete information from all operational sites. Specifically, in 2024, consumption at the Cali
                                                                                                                             Main Building – Tower 1 was recorded for only six months, whereas in 2025, data for the full twelve
                                                                                                                             months of the year was included, resulting in an upward variation compared to the previous period.
                                                                                                                             In this regard, the trend observed in the graph does not reflect a structural increase in water use, but
                                                                                                                             rather a more accurate and representative measurement of actual consumption, strengthening the
                                                                                                                             information base for implementing water optimization and efficient use measures in future periods.

Waste Generation
The trend in waste generated reflects the impact of the Bank’s operational activities and specific events, such
as building and office remodeling projects. In 2025, total waste generated was 246,66 tons, representing
a 25,94% reduction compared to 2024, a year in which a significant increase was recorded, primarily
associated with facility adaptation and renovation projects.
During 2025, 98,11% of the waste generated was properly treated and recycled, maintaining a performance
consistent with the past four years and demonstrating the effectiveness of our management. Given the nature
of our operations, approximately 80% of the waste generated is non-hazardous, most of which is recycled
or reused.                                                                                                                                Waste Not Sent to Landfill (Recovery)
                                                                                                                                          Waste recovery is a central pillar of our management and a reflection of the circular economy approach we
                                                                                                                                          promote in our operations. In 2025, more than 95% of the waste generated was recovered, maintaining a
      Overall, the 2025 results confirm a return to the path of waste reduction and                                                       performance consistent with recent years and demonstrating the effectiveness of the actions implemented.
      progress toward meeting the goals established in our Eco-Efficiency Plan.                                                           Non-hazardous waste accounts for the largest proportion of recovery. In 2025, 220,94 tons of recovered
                                                                                                                                          non-hazardous waste were managed, primarily paper, cardboard, wood, metal, and plastic—materials
                                                                                                                                          largely associated with building and office renovation processes—which were reintroduced into recycling
                                                                                                                                          chains through authorized environmental management companies.
     Waste destined for disposal
     Waste not destined for disposal                                                                                                      Regarding recycled hazardous waste, 21,06 tons were managed in 2025, with a notable reduction compared
                                                                                                                                          to 2024, particularly in Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE), as a result of the completion
                                                                                                                                          of technology renewal projects. Other waste, such as lamps and toner, continued to be managed under
                                                                                                                                          specialized recycling programs.

For the Loans Clan, the responsible marketing
approach is reinforced due to the impact that
credit products can have on customers’ financial
situations. Therefore, the Bank adopts strict criteria
of transparency, adequacy, and balance in the
information disclosed, promoting responsible
borrowing and avoiding practices that may encourage
over-indebtedness.

               Acknowledgments
               At Banco de Occidente, we know that sustainability cannot be achieved
               alone: it is built on trust, purpose, and the daily efforts of many people. In a
               challenging year, the constant support of our stakeholders drove us to keep
               moving forward with responsibility, empathy, and a vision for the future.
               We thank our employees for their commitment; our customers for their trust;
               our shareholders for supporting our strategy; our suppliers and strategic
               partners for their outstanding collaboration; the communities for allowing us
               to grow alongside them; and the authorities for their guidance and ongoing
               coordination.
               This report is our commitment to transparency and accountability: a way
               of sharing where we stand, what we have learned, and where we are headed.
               We will continue to contribute to a more sustainable transition and to our
               blue planet, convinced that every responsible decision counts and that the
               future is built better when we do it together. Thank you for being part of this
               journey.

                                                           secure, and the internal security protocol and crisis management team were activated.

                                                           Cybersecurity
                                                           Our management is supported by an information security framework that brings together guidelines, practices, and
                                                           controls to protect our clients’ and the Bank’s information. To remain aligned with recognized best practices, we use
                                                           international standards such as ISO 27001:2022, NIST 800-53 (v2.0), and local regulations such as the regulatory
                                                           circulars issued by the Colombian Financial Superintendency regarding compliance with security and cybersecurity
                                                           controls. We periodically review our approach to adapt it to changes in the environment and the evolution of our digital
                                                           services.
                                                           We also test our capabilities. We complement our internal audit and corporate compliance functions with assessment
                     FN-CB-230a.2 Description of                                                                                                                                                                    Information
                                                           exercises that help us identify opportunities for improvement and prioritize actions. In recent processes, we shared the
                     the approach to identifying                                                                                                                                          107 -                     security,
       SASB                                                results of an external assessment conducted in 2024 with the consulting firm Ernest & Young (EY), and during 2025 we
                     and addressing data security                                                                                                                                          108                      cybersecurity, and
                                                           made progress on a new assessment with Deloitte, which was ongoing at the end of the period.
                     risks                                                                                                                                                                                          system availability
                                                           Under the leadership of the Vice Presidency of Operations and Technology, together with the Vice Presidency of Risk,
                                                           technical and risk management teams are coordinated, taking into account the risk assessment model (ANX-APY-1186).
                                                           Monthly follow-ups are managed with the Information Security Committee, guided by the principle of continuous
                                                           improvement.
                                                           In 2025, we strengthened our prevention efforts with a simple principle: “the earlier we identify a risk, the lower its
                                                           impact.” That is why we combine controls, monitoring, and continuous improvements to protect information and
                                                           maintain the stability of our services. This approach allows us to act before a threat becomes an incident and to
                                                           support the growth of our digital channels with confidence.

                                                           In accordance with Circular Letter 068 of 2025 from the Financial Superintendency of Colombia (SFC) and in
                                                           compliance with paragraph 2.1.1.4.3 of Decree 2555 of 2010, the SFC published the list of Systemically Important
                     FN-CB-550a.1 Score in                 Institutions (SIIs) for fiscal year 2026, based on the methodology defined for their identification. For this calculation,                                 Ethical

                     assessment, by category               With these results, we ranked third, with a score of 9,58%, above the threshold of 6,45%, meaning that for the first
                                                           time we were considered a systemically important bank. It is important to note that this classification does not
                                                           represent a risk assessment or rating of the institutions.
                                                           In this context, the Bank must continue to build the additional buffer for systemic institutions, equivalent to 1% of
                                                           assets weighted for credit, market, and operational risk, in accordance with the instructions and deadlines issued by
                                                           the SFC in Resolution No. 2629 of December 27, 2024.
